# E — BFF core: commercetools client, session, env guards, identity core

**Specs:** `authentication-and-identity` (core only: session boundary, anonymous vs customer sessions; the four sign-in/reset scenarios are built in R), `storefront-project-bootstrap` (scenarios "Required environment variable missing", "Session secret too weak", "Secret never reaches the browser", "Connection check available in development only"), `storefront-code-structure` (scenario "Session carries no commercetools credential")
**Depends on:** A, B · **Unblocks:** F, H, I, K, L, R, U (generated by verify-plan) · **Decisions:** D-001, D-002, D-030, D-031, D-033, D-035, D-059
**Owner prerequisites:** OA-02 for live checks (unit tests need nothing) · **Skill refs:** `commercetools-platform` (SDK setup, ClientBuilder, client-credentials flow), `commercetools-storefront` (BFF, session patterns)

## Goal
The only door to commercetools exists and is guarded: validated env with fail-fast and weak-secret refusal, one SDK client, one signed session cookie that carries no commercetools credential, a shared API error shape, a dev-only health route, and mechanical guards (`check:secrets`, `check:bundle`, `check:dev-routes`) in `npm run verify`.

## Design

### Environment (`lib/ct/env-core.ts` pure, `lib/ct/env.ts` server-only)
`env-core.ts` has **no** `server-only` import (so `next.config.ts` and `instrumentation.ts` can import it; B's boundary check exempts it). `env.ts` is `import 'server-only'; export * from './env-core';`. App code imports `@/lib/ct/env`.
```ts
export type Env = {
  CTP_PROJECT_KEY: string; CTP_AUTH_URL: string; CTP_API_URL: string;
  CTP_CLIENT_ID: string; CTP_CLIENT_SECRET: string; CTP_SCOPES: string;
  SESSION_SECRET: string; CTP_CHECKOUT_APP_KEY?: string;
};
export type EnvSource = Record<string, string | undefined>;
export function validateEnv(source?: EnvSource, opts?: { requireCheckout?: boolean }): Env;
export function getCheckoutAppKey(source?: EnvSource): string;   // throws `Missing environment variable: CTP_CHECKOUT_APP_KEY`
export function getRegion(apiUrl: string): string;               // 'https://api.us-central1.gcp.commercetools.com' → 'us-central1.gcp'
export function flag(source: EnvSource, name: string, fallback = false): boolean; // 'true' | '1' → true
export function shouldValidateAtBuild(source?: EnvSource): boolean; // source.NETLIFY === 'true'
export const SESSION_SECRET_MIN = 32;
```
Rules (exact messages; **never** print a value):
- Required: `CTP_PROJECT_KEY, CTP_AUTH_URL, CTP_API_URL, CTP_CLIENT_ID, CTP_CLIENT_SECRET, CTP_SCOPES, SESSION_SECRET` — first missing or empty one in this order → `throw new Error('Missing environment variable: NAME')`.
- `CTP_CHECKOUT_APP_KEY` is optional in `validateEnv()` (the Checkout application exists only after OA-05) and required when `opts.requireCheckout` (Y's Netlify build uses it) or when U calls `getCheckoutAppKey()`. Planner default.
- `SESSION_SECRET` shorter than 32 characters → `throw new Error('SESSION_SECRET must be at least 32 characters')` in **every** environment (also development): the app never signs with a weak secret. The only exception is `NODE_ENV === 'test'` (Vitest), where an **unset** secret resolves to the constant `'test-only-session-secret-0123456789abcdef'` inside `lib/ct/session.ts`, never elsewhere.
- Any variable named `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` whose name contains `CTP`, `SECRET`, `SESSION`, `SEED` or `PEXELS` → `throw new Error('Secret-like variable must not carry the public prefix: NAME')` (name only).
- `validateEnv` returns only the typed fields (no passthrough of other variables).
**When it runs (Planner default):** `instrumentation.ts` at `site/` root: `register()` calls `validateEnv()` when `NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs'` and `NODE_ENV === 'production'` (so `next start` stops, naming the variable); `next.config.ts` calls `validateEnv(process.env, { requireCheckout: true })` when `shouldValidateAtBuild()` (Netlify builds fail by name); in development and in a local `npm run build` nothing is validated up front (so `npm run verify` works without OA-02) and the first commercetools call throws the same error. Add `README` section "Environment variables" listing every variable, secret or not, and where it is set (`site/.env.local` locally, Netlify UI later).

### API errors (`lib/api-error.ts` client-safe; `lib/ct/http.ts` server-only)
```ts
export const API_ERROR_STATUS = {
  VALIDATION: 400, UNAUTHENTICATED: 401, FORBIDDEN: 403, NOT_FOUND: 404, CONFLICT: 409,
  RATE_LIMITED: 429, INTERNAL: 500, UPSTREAM_ERROR: 502,
} as const;
export type ApiErrorCode = keyof typeof API_ERROR_STATUS;
export type ApiErrorBody = { error: { code: ApiErrorCode; message: string; details?: Record<string, unknown> } };
export class ApiError extends Error { constructor(public code: ApiErrorCode, message: string, public details?: Record<string, unknown>); get status(): number }
```
`lib/ct/http.ts`: `json(data, init?)` (adds `cache-control: no-store`), `errorResponse(err: unknown): NextResponse` — `ApiError` → its status and body; an SDK error with `statusCode` 404 → `NOT_FOUND`, 409 (ConcurrentModification) → `CONFLICT`, 400 → `VALIDATION` with message `Invalid request`, other 4xx/5xx or network → `UPSTREAM_ERROR` (502) with message `The service is temporarily unavailable`; anything else → `INTERNAL`. **Never** put the upstream body, stack or credentials in a response; log `console.error(err)` server-side without request headers. D's `/api/locale` already writes the same JSON shape literally. R may add `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`-style domain codes only by appending to `API_ERROR_STATUS` in its own task.

### Client (`lib/ct/client.ts`, server-only)
```ts
export function getApiRoot(): ByProjectKeyRequestBuilder;   // lazy singleton: one ClientBuilder per process
export function getProjectKey(): string; export function getApiUrl(): string; export function getAuthUrl(): string;
```
Built lazily on first call (never at import time, so `next build` needs no credentials): `new ClientBuilder().withProjectKey(key).withClientCredentialsFlow({ host: CTP_AUTH_URL, projectKey, credentials: { clientId, clientSecret }, scopes: CTP_SCOPES.split(' ').filter(Boolean) }).withHttpMiddleware({ host: CTP_API_URL }).build()`, then `createApiBuilderFromCtpClient(client).withProjectKey({ projectKey })` — pattern of `commercetools-platform` sdk-setup and the TS SDK docs ([docs](https://docs.commercetools.com/sdk/typescript-sdk)). All other modules `import { getApiRoot } from '@/lib/ct/client'`. This is the **only** file (plus `scripts/seed/lib.ts` for the admin seed client, F) allowed to import `@commercetools/ts-client` (B lint). The client is restricted (storefront scopes of OA-02); the seed credential is never configured here.

### Session (`lib/session-types.ts` client-safe; `lib/ct/session.ts` server-only) — decision D-030
Stateless **signed JWT cookie** (jose, HS256). It stores references, **never a commercetools credential**: no access token, no client credential, no password, no PII beyond the customer id. The BFF acts for the customer with its own restricted client and scopes each query by the `customerId` from the verified cookie (so no customer bearer token is held anywhere; Planner default for the spec's open question — a server-side session store is not needed).
```ts
export type SessionData = {
  anonymousId?: string;     // uuid (crypto.randomUUID) minted when an anonymous visitor first needs a cart
  customerId?: string;      // present only when signed in
  cartId?: string;          // reference to the active cart
  lastOrderNumber?: string; // U: lets a guest open its own confirmation page (D-035)
  locale?: string; country?: string; currency?: string; // market snapshot at last write; NOT authoritative (use getMarket() from D)
};
export type SessionKind = 'none' | 'anonymous' | 'customer';
export type SessionSummary = { kind: SessionKind; customerId?: string; hasCart: boolean };
```
`lib/ct/session.ts` exports:
```ts
export const SESSION_COOKIE = 'malva-session';
export const SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS = 2_592_000; // 30 days, fixed (not sliding)
export const SESSION_FIELDS: readonly (keyof SessionData)[]; // the whitelist
export async function createSessionToken(data: SessionData): Promise<string>;   // keeps ONLY whitelisted fields, drops undefined; HS256; iat; exp = 30 days
export async function getSession(): Promise<SessionData>;                       // {} for no cookie, tampered, wrong algorithm or expired
export function setSessionCookie(res: NextResponse, token: string): void;
export function clearSessionCookie(res: NextResponse): void;
export async function updateSession(patch: Partial<SessionData>, res: NextResponse): Promise<SessionData>; // merge → re-sign → set cookie; undefined deletes a field
```
Cookie: name `malva-session`, `httpOnly: true`, `sameSite: 'lax'`, `path: '/'`, `maxAge: 2592000`, `secure: NODE_ENV === 'production'`. Secret: `SESSION_SECRET` through `validateSessionSecret` (env-core): shorter than 32 → throws `SESSION_SECRET must be at least 32 characters`; unset → throws `Missing environment variable: SESSION_SECRET` except `NODE_ENV === 'test'` (constant above). `jwtVerify(..., { algorithms: ['HS256'] })` (rejects `alg: none`).
`lib/ct/identity.ts` (server-only):
```ts
export function sessionKind(s: SessionData): SessionKind;            // customerId → 'customer'; else anonymousId or cartId → 'anonymous'; else 'none'
export function requireCustomer(s: SessionData): string;             // returns customerId or throws new ApiError('UNAUTHENTICATED', 'Sign in required')
export function ensureAnonymousId(s: SessionData): { anonymousId: string; created: boolean };
export function toSummary(s: SessionData): SessionSummary;
```
Anonymous vs customer: a visitor is **anonymous** while it only has `anonymousId` (+ optional `cartId`); signing in (R) sets `customerId`, keeps `cartId` per the merge result and removes `anonymousId`; signing out (R) clears the cookie. Guest checkout is allowed (D-035). Nothing in E calls commercetools sign-in, password-reset or email-token endpoints: those flows (global customers, commercetools-owned passwords, auto-verification, demo reset link, D-030/D-031/D-033) are built in R.

### Rate limiter (`lib/rate-limit.ts`, `lib/config/rateLimits.ts`) — Planner default for the spec's "who rate-limits sign-in" question
`rateLimit(key: string, opts: { limit: number; windowMs: number }, now = Date.now()): { ok: boolean; retryAfterSeconds: number }` — fixed window, in-memory `Map` stored on `globalThis` (per-instance on serverless; accepted risk, noted in README). `clientKey(request: Request, route: string): string` — first IP of `x-nf-client-connection-ip`, else first of `x-forwarded-for`, else `unknown`, then `:` + route. `lib/config/rateLimits.ts` exports `RATE_LIMITS = { login: { limit: 10, windowMs: 60_000 }, register: { limit: 5, windowMs: 60_000 }, forgotPassword: { limit: 5, windowMs: 60_000 }, resetPassword: { limit: 5, windowMs: 60_000 } }`. R uses them and answers `429` with `ApiError('RATE_LIMITED', …)` and a `Retry-After` header.

### Reference vertical slice (the "one existing example per layer" for B's README)
- `lib/fetcher.ts` (client-safe): `fetchJson<T>(url: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<T>` and `sendJson<T>(url, method: 'POST'|'PUT'|'PATCH'|'DELETE', body?: unknown): Promise<T>`; non-OK responses throw the **client-side** `ApiError` (same class as `lib/api-error.ts`, status from the response, code/message from `{ error }`; network or non-JSON failures → `ApiError('UPSTREAM_ERROR', …)`).
- `app/api/auth/session/route.ts`: `GET` → `json({ session: toSummary(await getSession()) })`; no cookie is set by a GET.
- `hooks/useSession.ts` (`'use client'`): `useSession()` → `{ session: SessionSummary | undefined, isLoading, error, mutate }` using SWR key `'session'` (constant in `lib/cache-keys.ts`, created here: `export const KEY_SESSION = 'session'`; M appends `KEY_CART`) and `fetchJson`. Components call the hook, never `fetch`.

### Health and dev-only routes (`.dev.ts` extension from A)
- `app/api/health/route.dev.ts` — `GET`: `await getApiRoot().get().execute()` (Get Project, [docs](https://docs.commercetools.com/api/projects/project#get-project); needs scope `view_project_settings`, present in OA-02) → `200 { "ok": true, "projectKey": "<key from the response body>", "region": getRegion(CTP_API_URL) }`; any error → `500 { "ok": false, "error": "<error name only, no message body>" }`. Present in `next dev`, **absent from the production build** (Next 16 verified: `route.dev.ts` is excluded because `pageExtensions` has no `dev.ts` in production; see A).
- `app/api/dev/session/route.dev.ts` — `POST` body `{ "kind": "anonymous" | "customer" | "clear" }`: sets a test session cookie (`anonymous` → `ensureAnonymousId`; `customer` → `customerId: 'dev-customer'`; `clear` → clears) so Claude can inspect cookie flags before R exists. Dev-only.
- `scripts/check-dev-routes.mjs` (E-10): after `npm run build`, fails if `.next/server/app/api/health`, `.next/server/app/api/dev` or `.next/server/app/dev` exist, or any `route.dev.*` / `page.dev.*` file is listed in `.next/server/app-paths-manifest.json`. Exports `checkDevRoutes(siteDir): string[]`.

### Secret guards
`scripts/check-secrets.mjs` — exports `checkSecrets(rootDir: string): string[]` (rootDir = `site/`; uses `git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard`, falls back to a directory walk outside git; ignores `node_modules`, `.next`, `.git`; never prints a secret value):
- (a) any tracked source file outside `scripts/` and `*.test.*` containing a match of `NEXT_PUBLIC_[A-Z0-9_]*(CTP|SESSION|SECRET|SEED|PEXELS)` → `file: contains NEXT_PUBLIC_… (server secrets must never be public)`;
- (b) `.env.example` (and `.env.seed.example` if present) has a non-empty value for `CTP_CLIENT_ID`, `CTP_CLIENT_SECRET`, `SESSION_SECRET`, `CTP_CHECKOUT_APP_KEY`, `CTP_SEED_CLIENT_ID`, `CTP_SEED_CLIENT_SECRET` → `.env.example: NAME must be empty`; and `.env.example` mentions any `CTP_SEED_` name → `.env.example: seed credentials must not be configured for site/`;
- (c) a tracked file whose basename starts with `.env` other than `.env.example` and `.env.seed.example` → `file: env file must not be tracked`;
- (d) in `.ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs` outside `scripts/` and tests, a quoted literal of ≥ 32 characters assigned to `SESSION_SECRET` or `CLIENT_SECRET` (regex `\b(SESSION_SECRET|CLIENT_SECRET)\b\s*[:=]\s*(['"`])[^'"`\n]{32,}\2`) → `file: string literal assigned to a secret variable`.
`scripts/check-bundle-secrets.mjs` — exports `scanBundle(dir: string, env: Record<string, string | undefined>): string[]`: walks `.next/static/**` (all files, read as latin1) and reports `file: contains the name X` for each of `CLIENT_SECRET`, `SESSION_SECRET`, `CTP_SEED`, `PEXELS_API_KEY`, and `file: contains the value of NAME` for the values of `CTP_CLIENT_SECRET`, `CTP_CLIENT_ID`, `SESSION_SECRET` and, when `site/.env.seed` exists, `CTP_SEED_CLIENT_ID`, `CTP_SEED_CLIENT_SECRET` (values never echoed). A missing directory is itself a problem (`bundle directory not found (run the build first)`). The CLI loads `.env.local` and `.env.seed` with `process.loadEnvFile` when present. If a third-party library legitimately contains one of the names, record it in `plan/QUESTIONS.md`; do not weaken the check.
npm scripts and positions in `verify` (canonical table in A): `check:secrets` (step 1), `check:bundle` (step 10), `check:dev-routes` (step 11).

### Pitfalls
- `server-only` throws when imported outside the React server condition: that is why `env-core.ts` has no such import and `next.config.ts` / `instrumentation.ts` import only `env-core`.
- Never build the commercetools client at module top level: `next build` would need credentials.
- `cookies()` from `next/headers` is async in Next 16: `(await cookies()).get(...)`.
- Route handlers that set cookies must set them on the `NextResponse` they return (`updateSession(patch, res)`), not on `cookies()`.
- A JWT is signed, not encrypted: that is why only references are stored. Do not add emails or names to it.
- `jose` rejects unknown algorithms only if you pass `algorithms`; always pass `['HS256']`.
- The `.dev.ts` trick works only because A's `pageExtensions` is conditional on `NODE_ENV`; do not rename these files to `route.ts`.

| Scenario (exact title from the spec) | Capability | Test (file → `it(...)` name) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Required environment variable missing | `storefront-project-bootstrap` | `lib/ct/env.test.ts` → "Required environment variable missing: names the variable and prints no value of a present one" and `instrumentation.test.ts` → "Required environment variable missing: register() stops a production start naming the variable" |
| Session secret too weak | `storefront-project-bootstrap` | `lib/ct/env.test.ts` → "Session secret too weak: 31 characters is refused" and `lib/ct/session.test.ts` → "Session secret too weak: the session module refuses to sign with it" |
| Secret never reaches the browser | `storefront-project-bootstrap` | `scripts/check-bundle-secrets.test.ts` → "Secret never reaches the browser: a planted secret name or value in .next/static fails the check" and `scripts/check-secrets.test.ts` → "Secret never reaches the browser: a NEXT_PUBLIC_ secret variable is reported" |
| Connection check available in development only | `storefront-project-bootstrap` | `scripts/check-dev-routes.test.ts` → "Connection check available in development only: a production build containing api/health fails the check" and `app/api/health/route.dev.test.ts` → "Connection check available in development only: returns the project key when the API answers" |
| Session carries no commercetools credential | `storefront-code-structure` | `lib/ct/session.test.ts` → "Session carries no commercetools credential: only whitelisted reference fields are signed, the cookie is HttpOnly and tamper-proof" |

## Chrome verification (run by Claude)
- C-E-1 (needs OA-02, A, B): `http://localhost:3000/api/health` in `npm run dev` → JSON `{"ok":true,"projectKey":"spec-test-b2c-telecom","region":"us-central1.gcp"}`, status 200, `content-type: application/json`; body contains no client id, secret or token; console clean.
- C-E-2 (needs A, B): `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/session` → `{"session":{"kind":"none","hasCart":false}}`, header `cache-control: no-store`, no `Set-Cookie` in the response.
- C-E-3 (needs A, B): on that origin run `evaluate_script` `fetch('/api/dev/session',{method:'POST',headers:{'content-type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify({kind:'anonymous'})})` → network entry shows `Set-Cookie: malva-session=…; Path=/; Max-Age=2592000; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax` (no `Secure` on localhost development); `document.cookie` does not contain `malva-session`; decode the JWT payload (base64url middle part) → keys are only `anonymousId`, `iat`, `exp`; header `alg` is `HS256`; then GET `/api/auth/session` → `{"session":{"kind":"anonymous","hasCart":false}}`.
- C-E-4 (needs A, B): `POST /api/dev/session` with `{"kind":"clear"}` → cookie expires (`Max-Age=0`); GET `/api/auth/session` → kind `none`.
- C-E-5 (needs OA-02, A, B): `npm run build && npm run start -- -p 3010` with a complete `.env.local` → `http://localhost:3010/api/health` returns 404 and `http://localhost:3010/api/dev/session` returns 404; `.next/server/app/api/health` does not exist (terminal evidence); `http://localhost:3010/api/auth/session` still answers 200.
- C-E-6 (needs A, B): terminal then browser — start production with `SESSION_SECRET=short npm run start -- -p 3011` → the process exits non-zero with `SESSION_SECRET must be at least 32 characters` and no value echoed; in Chrome `http://localhost:3011/` fails to connect. Repeat with `CTP_CLIENT_SECRET` unset → message `Missing environment variable: CTP_CLIENT_SECRET`.

## Excluded
Built in R (page or flow scenarios of `authentication-and-identity`, each listed by its exact title):
- Sign in carries the anonymous cart — built in R (login route, `anonymousCartSignInMode`, cart merge; E provides only the session fields `anonymousId`/`cartId`/`customerId`).
- Failed sign in is ambiguous — built in R (generic message, `/api/auth/login`).
- Password reset does not confirm the email — built in R; under D-033 the link is shown on screen only in demo mode, never emailed (D-031: no email at all).
- Verification before recovery — built in R; under D-031 new accounts are auto-verified, so the flow only states what is required for unverified legacy accounts.
Also not built here: sign-out, registration, any sign-in form or page (R).
